A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConceptPose. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation experiments on four datasets, few-shot tracking results, and multiple main-text and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a binary-mask ablation, occlusion analysis, and qualitative concept-localization studies.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains LLM concept generation, VLM saliency extraction, 3D projection, softmax concept vectors, KL-based matching, RANSAC, and ICP. The new binary-mask configuration is an experimental ablation; the proposed method remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on LINEMOD-Occlusion in supplementary Section 10 and a car-object qualitative example in Section 9. The original four benchmark datasets and YCB-Video tracking task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 10 adds an internal comparator using concept masks binarized at threshold 0.5. External comparator memberships in Tables 1 and 4 remain unchanged; the new comparison does not evaluate a separate segmentation system.

E3.justification: New experiments specify a 0.5 binarization threshold, a car comparison using 3, 10, and 15 concepts, and 20 randomly sampled anchor-query pairs per LINEMOD-Occlusion object. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, settings, and tracking procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Supplementary Sections 8–11 substantially expand the analyses: they test continuous versus binary representations, examine occlusion versus pose error, illustrate concept quantity on a car, and visualize cross-instance camera concept localization. The original prompt, backbone, quantity, correspondence, voxelization, and per-object analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces regression-based analysis of occlusion and ADD-S error, reporting R² = 0.288 in Figure 7. The fixed RANSAC seed remains 42, and neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their results. New Table 10 reports ADD(-S)/BOP AR of 71.5/60.4 for continuous vectors versus 30.5/28.2 for binary masks. v3 also adds the occlusion scatter plot and car/camera qualitative findings; these are additional results, not improved scores on the retained benchmarks.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for pose composition, concept normalization, KL similarity, and correspondence selection are unchanged. The new point-versus-line degrees-of-freedom analogy is explanatory prose, without a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The training-free, CAD-model-free contribution and performance claims are retained. v3 clarifies the abstract's approximately 62% advantage as a relative improvement in average ADD(-S) over the strongest baseline, consistent with v1's existing Table 1 and Section 4.4.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of continuous activations, repeated parts, and cropping/masking/RANSAC as sources of reliable correspondence or occlusion robustness. It also interprets R² below 0.3 as no linear correlation and claims cross-instance advantages over learned descriptors. Existing runtime, viewpoint, and severe-occlusion limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL on the first page. Existing hardware, software, backbone-layer details, prompts, RANSAC parameters, and evaluation-pair publication statements are retained. The PDFs establish the added access pointer, without establishing the contents of the linked resource.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tian et al., Learning a Category-Level Object Pose Estimator Without Pose Annotations, to the category-level discussion. The broad research positioning remains stable; most other reference changes update bibliographic information or consolidate the duplicate FreeZe citation.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely unchanged. v3 clarifies the abstract, edits author affiliation/contact information and bibliographic entries, and adds four short supplementary sections. The former Extended Qualitative Results section becomes Section 12 with essentially unchanged wording.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 10 and Figures 6–8, with localized layout reflow. The original extended qualitative panels are preserved as Figures 9–10, previously Figures 6–7; the other existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 10 provides useful direct evidence for the central choice of continuous concept vectors, and the added visual examples clarify their behavior. The gain is limited by the new occlusion analysis: R² = 0.288 does not establish no linear correlation, and Figure 7 describes per-object subplots while displaying one scatter plot. These weaknesses temper the added support; the core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
